A memorable boss asks the player to notice spacing, timing, stamina, aggression or defensive habits, then applies enough pressure that those lessons matter. When difficulty feels arbitrary, frustration replaces learning. When it feels structured, the encounter becomes a conversation between the game’s rules and the player’s response.
contentBlocks.heading: Difficulty Is a Tool, Not the Whole Point

contentBlocks.text: Bosses such as Genichiro in Sekiro or Margit in Elden Ring work partly because they expose habits. Genichiro pressures players to engage with deflection and initiative, while Margit disrupts panic dodges with delayed timings and varied attack rhythms. The first attempt can feel overwhelming, but later attempts often become more legible because the player is building a mental model of the encounter.
contentBlocks.heading: The Best Fights Teach Through Repetition

contentBlocks.text: Animation is not only mechanical information. The way a boss moves can communicate discipline, desperation, weight, speed or instability before the story explains anything directly. FromSoftware often lets posture and attack rhythm carry characterization, which is why learning a moveset can also feel like learning something about the person or creature performing it.
contentBlocks.heading: Movesets Communicate Character

contentBlocks.text: The arena quietly controls how a boss feels. Open spaces encourage movement and repositioning; tighter rooms create pressure; elevation, pillars or environmental boundaries can change how safe each decision feels. Strong encounters use that space deliberately so the battlefield becomes part of the boss’s identity rather than a neutral backdrop.
contentBlocks.heading: Arenas Shape the Rhythm of the Fight

contentBlocks.text: FromSoftware’s own sound-design staff has described receiving boss concepts and background information before composing Elden Ring boss music. That connection matters. A soundtrack can turn a mechanical escalation into a dramatic one, while attack sounds and impact cues reinforce timing and threat. The fight becomes easier to remember because its mechanical rhythm and emotional tone arrive together.
contentBlocks.heading: Music and Sound Give Mechanics Emotional Weight

contentBlocks.text: A strong second phase does more than make numbers larger. It changes the meaning of familiar patterns by adding reach, speed, new positioning demands or a different tempo. The player enters with knowledge from the first phase but has to reinterpret it under new conditions. That mixture of recognition and disruption is one of the studio’s most reliable ways to create escalation.
contentBlocks.heading: Phase Changes Reframe What You Already Learned

contentBlocks.text: Not every encounter needs maximum scale. FromSoftware mixes duels, monsters, puzzle-like encounters and large set pieces, which makes the peaks stand out. A restrained one-on-one fight can be as memorable as a giant spectacle because the studio changes what kind of attention the player needs to bring from one boss to the next.
contentBlocks.heading: Contrast Keeps Spectacle From Becoming Routine

contentBlocks.text: The final reason these encounters stick is that the player remembers their own improvement. A boss that once seemed unreadable can eventually feel precise and manageable. The victory matters because the experience contains a before-and-after version of the player: the person who did not understand the fight, and the person who finally did.
contentBlocks.heading: Mastery Turns the Fight Into a Personal Story

quickRead: FromSoftware’s strongest boss encounters teach recognizable patterns instead of relying only on spectacle or difficulty.
Presentation, music, arena design and narrative context make the best encounters memorable before and after the mechanical test.
Phase changes work best when they extend an encounter’s existing language instead of discarding what the player has already learned.
conclusion:
FromSoftware’s boss design works when mechanics, presentation and learning all point in the same direction. Difficulty creates pressure, but readability creates progress; music and animation give the encounter personality; phases and arenas shape its rhythm; repetition gives the player time to understand it.

That is why the studio’s strongest fights remain memorable long after the exact number of attempts is forgotten. The lasting memory is not simply that the boss was hard. It is that the fight changed from confusion into understanding, and that transformation felt like part of the drama itself.
conclusionHeading: The best bosses make learning feel dramatic

title: Elden Ring Best Starting Class for Beginners: All 12 Classes Explained
description: The best Elden Ring starting classes for beginners, including Vagabond, Samurai, Astrologer and the new Heavy Knight and Idus Knight options added in 2026.
body:
Elden Ring asks you to choose a starting class before you know exactly how you want to play. The good news is that the choice is much less permanent than it first appears. Your class determines your opening level, attribute spread and equipment, but it does not lock your character into a fixed role for the rest of the game.

For most first-time players, **Vagabond remains the safest overall starting class** because its high Vigor and balanced physical stats give you more room to learn the game. Samurai is an excellent alternative for players who want a faster, more flexible opening, while Astrologer is the clearest starting point for sorcery-focused characters.

There is also a new 2026 consideration. Elden Ring's original ten classes have been joined by **Heavy Knight** and **Idus Knight** through the Tarnished Pack. Those two classes are included with Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 and are available as additional paid content on the other current platforms. They expand the choices, but new players do not need them to build a strong first character.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition key art showing a Tarnished against the game’s dark fantasy landscape.
imageCredit: Bandai Namco Entertainment / FromSoftware

contentBlocks.text:
A starting class mainly changes your opening attributes, starting level and initial equipment. It does **not** decide what your character is allowed to become later.

That matters because beginners often spend too long trying to predict an endgame build before they have played enough to know what they enjoy. A better approach is to choose a class that gives you a comfortable first few hours, then develop your character around the systems and playstyle you actually prefer.

At equivalent levels, classes do not gain extra hidden attribute points simply because they began at a higher level. The practical difference is where those points are concentrated at the start. For a first playthrough, survivability and clarity are usually more valuable than perfect long-term optimization.

For a broader first-hours overview, read Neural Critic’s [Elden Ring beginner’s guide](/stories/elden-ring-beginners-guide/).
contentBlocks.heading: What does your starting class actually change?

contentBlocks.text:
**Vagabond is the easiest class to recommend to a first-time Elden Ring player.** It begins at level 9 with 15 Vigor, the highest Vigor value among the original starting classes, plus a balanced spread of Strength and Dexterity.

That extra health is useful because it gives you more time to understand why an encounter went wrong. Elden Ring is a game where learning enemy timing, stamina management and positioning matters more than squeezing every possible point of damage out of an early build.

Vagabond also leaves you plenty of room to specialize later. You can move toward Strength, Dexterity or a mixed physical setup without feeling as though your starting choice is fighting against you.
contentBlocks.heading: Best overall starting class for beginners: Vagabond

contentBlocks.text:
Samurai is one of the strongest alternatives for beginners who want a quicker and more agile physical start. It begins with 12 Vigor, 13 Endurance and 15 Dexterity, giving it a useful combination of survivability, stamina and Dexterity from the opening minutes.

The biggest advantage is flexibility. Samurai has enough durability to be approachable without being as specialized as a pure caster or Faith class, and its starting attributes naturally support several different physical directions later.

If Vagabond sounds a little too defensive or straightforward, Samurai is the next class we would put in front of a new player.
contentBlocks.heading: Best flexible alternative: Samurai

contentBlocks.text:
Astrologer is the clearest choice for players who already know they want to build around sorcery. It starts with 16 Intelligence and 15 Mind, far ahead of the more physical classes in the attributes most relevant to that style.

The tradeoff is durability. Astrologer starts with only 9 Vigor, so mistakes are less forgiving than they are with Vagabond or Hero. That does not make Astrologer a bad beginner class; it simply means the opening teaches a different lesson. Positioning, resource management and keeping space between yourself and danger matter more immediately.

For someone specifically excited by Elden Ring's magic systems, Astrologer is still the most direct starting point.
contentBlocks.heading: Best starting class for sorcery: Astrologer

contentBlocks.text:
Confessor is our preferred Faith-oriented starting class for a beginner because it is less narrowly specialized than Prophet. It begins with 14 Faith, 13 Mind and balanced physical attributes, which gives you room to mix incantations with a conventional physical playstyle while you learn how both sides of the character work.

Prophet starts with higher Faith at 16 and is the more efficient choice for someone who already knows they want a heavily Faith-focused character. Confessor, however, is easier to recommend when the player is still discovering what they enjoy.
contentBlocks.heading: Best Faith-oriented beginner class: Confessor

contentBlocks.text:
Patch 1.17 and the Tarnished Pack added two new starting classes in August 2026: **Heavy Knight** and **Idus Knight**. They are included by default with Elden Ring Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 and are available through the Tarnished Pack on PlayStation, Xbox and PC.

Heavy Knight begins at level 10 with **14 Vigor, 17 Endurance and 15 Strength**, making it an appealing starting point for players who want a durable physical character with a large early stamina and equip-load reserve. Its low Mind, Intelligence and Faith make its intended direction easy to read.

Idus Knight begins at level 7 with **15 Dexterity, 13 Strength, 12 Mind and 11 Faith**. That makes it more of a Dexterity-led hybrid than a pure specialist. Its 10 Vigor is noticeably less forgiving than Heavy Knight or Vagabond, so we would not put it ahead of those classes for a completely new player.

Neither class makes the original ten obsolete. They are additional starting profiles rather than straight upgrades.

For the current release context around these additions, see our [Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition coverage](/stories/elden-ring-tarnished-edition-91-metacritic-switch-2/).
contentBlocks.heading: Heavy Knight and Idus Knight: the two new 2026 classes

contentBlocks.text:
For a first playthrough, we would group the classes like this:

**Best overall beginner choice:** Vagabond  
**Best flexible physical alternative:** Samurai  
**Best durable Tarnished Pack option:** Heavy Knight  
**Best sorcery start:** Astrologer  
**Best beginner Faith hybrid:** Confessor  
**Best pure Strength start among the original classes:** Hero  
**Best pure Faith specialist:** Prophet  
**Best Dexterity/Intelligence hybrid:** Prisoner  
**Best new Dexterity-led hybrid:** Idus Knight  
**More specialized choices:** Warrior and Bandit  
**Best for players who deliberately want a blank-slate challenge:** Wretch

None of these labels should be read as a permanent build restriction. They describe which starting profile is easiest to understand for a particular goal, not what your character must still look like dozens of hours later.
contentBlocks.heading: How all 12 starting classes fit together

contentBlocks.text:
If you have no firm build in mind, choose **Vagabond**. Its health and balanced physical attributes give you the largest margin for learning the game without committing too early.

Choose **Samurai** if you want a more agile physical start, **Astrologer** if sorcery is the main reason you are excited to play, and **Confessor** if Faith and incantations interest you but you still want a balanced opening.

If you own the Tarnished Pack, **Heavy Knight** is also a very beginner-friendly physical option. Idus Knight is interesting for a more specialized Dexterity-led hybrid, but its lower Vigor makes it a less forgiving recommendation for a first character.

The only class we would actively steer most first-time players away from is **Wretch**. Starting at level 1 with an even attribute spread is useful for players who want maximum freedom or a deliberately sparse opening, but it removes many of the conveniences that make the first hours easier to read.

Once you have chosen a class, our [early-game progression guide](/stories/elden-ring-early-progression-what-to-upgrade-first/) explains what to prioritize next, while the [stats and soft-caps guide](/stories/elden-ring-stats-soft-caps-explained/) explains the attribute system in more detail.
contentBlocks.heading: Which Elden Ring class should you choose?

quickRead: Vagabond remains the easiest all-round starting class to recommend to most Elden Ring beginners.
Samurai is a flexible alternative, while Astrologer is the clearest starting point for a sorcery-focused character.
Heavy Knight and Idus Knight were added as new starting classes with the 2026 Tarnished Pack.
Starting class shapes your opening equipment and stats, but it does not permanently lock your character into one build.
conclusion:
For most beginners, **Vagabond is still the best Elden Ring starting class**. It gives you health, flexibility and enough physical strength to learn the game without forcing an early specialization.

Samurai is the strongest alternative for a flexible physical start, Astrologer is the best entry point for sorcery, and Confessor is our preferred Faith-oriented beginner choice. The 2026 Tarnished Pack adds two worthwhile options as well: Heavy Knight is especially friendly to players who want a durable physical opening, while Idus Knight is better suited to a more deliberate Dexterity-focused hybrid.

The important thing is not to treat character creation like a permanent contract. Pick the class that makes your first hours understandable, then let the Lands Between show you what kind of character you actually want to build.

title: Elden Ring Stats and Soft Caps Explained: Vigor, Mind, Endurance and More
description: A clear Elden Ring stat guide explaining what Vigor, Mind, Endurance, Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Faith and Arcane do, plus the soft caps that matter most.
body:
Elden Ring's attribute screen looks simple until you start asking the questions that actually matter: how much Vigor is enough, when does Endurance stop being efficient, and what does a "soft cap" really mean?

A soft cap is not a point where a stat suddenly stops working. It is a threshold where each additional level begins giving less value than it did before. Elden Ring uses several different scaling curves, so there is rarely one universal number that applies to every effect tied to an attribute.

For beginners, the most important principle is straightforward: **meet the requirements for the build you are actually using, invest in survivability, and only then push a damage-focused attribute toward its later breakpoints.** That approach is more useful than treating every soft-cap chart like a mandatory checklist.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: A Tarnished stands beneath the glowing Erdtree in Elden Ring, with ruined stone structures and the Lands Between below.
imageCredit: Neural Critic / Elden Ring gameplay screenshot.

contentBlocks.text:
A **soft cap** is the point where an attribute continues to improve your character, but each new level becomes less efficient than it was before.

That distinction matters. A soft cap is not the same as a hard cap, and it does not mean you should never level a stat beyond it. It simply tells you when the return per level changes enough that another attribute may be a better use of your next few levels.

Elden Ring also gives some attributes more than one important breakpoint. Vigor is the clearest example: HP growth is extremely strong before 40, still useful from 40 to 60, and much weaker after 60.

If you are still deciding how to begin, our [Elden Ring starting-class guide](/stories/elden-ring-best-starting-classes-beginners/) explains the 12 current opening classes.
contentBlocks.heading: What is a soft cap in Elden Ring?

contentBlocks.text:
Vigor determines maximum HP and also contributes to several defensive values. For most players, it is the easiest attribute to understand because the benefit is immediate: more health gives you more room to survive mistakes.

The important HP breakpoints are **40 Vigor** and **60 Vigor**. Returns are very strong on the way to 40, remain meaningful between 40 and 60, and fall sharply after 60.

For a first playthrough, that makes Vigor one of the safest early investments. You do not need to rush straight to 60, but reaching a comfortable health pool usually matters more than squeezing a small amount of extra damage out of an unfinished build.
contentBlocks.heading: Vigor: 40 and 60 are the big HP breakpoints

contentBlocks.text:
Mind increases FP, the resource used by spells, skills and several support systems. Unlike Vigor, there is no single beginner target that makes sense for every character because some builds spend very little FP while others depend on it constantly.

FP gains remain useful for a long stretch of investment, with diminishing returns becoming more noticeable toward the higher ranges. A common practical stopping area sits well below the maximum because the goal is usually to have enough FP for your normal combat rhythm rather than to chase the largest possible blue bar.

If you rarely run out of FP, adding more Mind is probably less useful than strengthening another part of the character.
contentBlocks.heading: Mind: useful, but more build-dependent

contentBlocks.text:
Endurance affects both **Stamina** and **Equip Load**, and those two benefits do not follow exactly the same curve.

Stamina gains slow significantly as Endurance rises, with a major practical breakpoint around **50 Endurance**. Equip Load continues gaining meaningful value further, reaching another important breakpoint around **60**.

Most ordinary builds do not need to approach either number. Endurance is usually best treated as a comfort stat: add enough to keep your stamina management comfortable and your chosen equipment within the load category you want.
contentBlocks.heading: Endurance: stamina and equip load do not cap at the same point

contentBlocks.text:
Strength and Dexterity both affect physical damage scaling, but the exact curve depends on how a particular build converts those attributes into damage.

For many standard scaling curves, the **mid-50s** are an important efficiency breakpoint and **80** is the major late-game soft cap. That does not mean every build should automatically stop at 55 or push to 80. Hybrid characters, lower-level characters and builds with other priorities may be better served by stopping earlier.

The practical rule is to avoid sacrificing Vigor, Endurance or another essential attribute simply to force a damage stat toward a later cap.
contentBlocks.heading: Strength and Dexterity: think in ranges, not one magic number

contentBlocks.text:
Intelligence and Faith govern access to their respective spell families and contribute to spell scaling, but their efficiency depends heavily on the casting setup being used.

For high-investment casting builds, **60** and **80** are the two numbers that appear most often as important late-game breakpoints. Some setups favor the lower end of that range while others continue scaling efficiently toward 80.

Beginners should treat those numbers as planning references, not immediate goals. First meet the requirements for the spells and systems you actually want to use, then raise the relevant attribute as the rest of the build becomes more stable.
contentBlocks.heading: Intelligence and Faith: casting breakpoints depend on your setup

contentBlocks.text:
Arcane is one of Elden Ring's more complicated attributes because it contributes to several different systems, including item discovery and certain forms of status buildup and damage scaling.

Because those effects use different curves, Arcane does not have one universal soft cap. **45** is an important breakpoint for some status-related scaling, while higher Arcane investment can remain useful for other effects into the 50–60 range and beyond.

That makes Arcane especially dependent on the purpose of the build. If you are not deliberately using systems that scale from Arcane, putting levels into it simply because the number is low is usually inefficient.
contentBlocks.heading: Arcane: several systems share one attribute

contentBlocks.text:
A useful leveling order for a new player is:

1. **Meet the minimum requirements** for the spells, equipment and systems you actually plan to use.  
2. **Raise Vigor** until mistakes stop feeling instantly fatal.  
3. Add **Endurance or Mind** if stamina, equip load or FP is regularly limiting you.  
4. Invest in the main offensive attribute that supports your chosen playstyle.  
5. Use soft caps as a signal to reassess the build rather than as a number you must reach.

This approach keeps the character functional at every stage instead of creating a high-damage stat sheet with obvious weaknesses elsewhere.

For a practical order of operations rather than a stat-by-stat reference, use our [Elden Ring early-game progression guide](/stories/elden-ring-early-progression-what-to-upgrade-first/).
contentBlocks.heading: A simple way to level without overthinking soft caps

contentBlocks.text:
These are the most useful general breakpoints to remember:

**Vigor:** 40 / 60 for HP  
**Mind:** gradual diminishing returns; build-dependent  
**Endurance:** around 50 for Stamina, around 60 for Equip Load  
**Strength:** commonly mid-50s / 80 for major damage-scaling breakpoints  
**Dexterity:** commonly mid-50s / 80 for major damage-scaling breakpoints  
**Intelligence:** commonly 60 / 80 for high-investment casting  
**Faith:** commonly 60 / 80 for high-investment casting  
**Arcane:** commonly around 45 for some status scaling, with other effects continuing higher

The exact point where a level becomes inefficient can vary because one attribute may affect several different derived stats. Treat the table as a planning map, not an absolute rule.

New to the wider game as well? Start with our [Elden Ring beginner’s guide](/stories/elden-ring-beginners-guide/) for exploration, checkpoints and other first-hours systems.
contentBlocks.heading: Soft-cap reference table

quickRead: Vigor has especially important practical breakpoints around 40 and 60 for most builds.
Strength and Dexterity commonly continue scaling meaningfully into the mid-50s and again toward 80, depending on the equipment and affinity used.
Intelligence and Faith often have major casting breakpoints around 60 and 80, while Arcane varies more by status and scaling setup.
Soft caps are diminishing-return points, not hard limits, so the right stopping point still depends on the build.
conclusion:
Soft caps are most useful when they stop you from wasting levels, not when they turn character building into a spreadsheet exercise.

For most players, the numbers worth remembering first are **40 and 60 Vigor**. After that, Mind and Endurance should solve actual resource problems, while offensive attributes should be pushed only as far as the build needs before their diminishing returns make another stat more valuable.

Elden Ring gives you enough freedom that there is rarely one perfect stat line. Use the soft caps to understand the tradeoffs, then build around the way you actually play.

title: Metro 2039 Release Date Confirmed, PS5 and Xbox 60fps Ray Tracing Detailed
description: Metro 2039 launches February 4, 2027. Here are the confirmed platforms, PS5 Pro details and 60fps ray-traced performance options on console.
body:
Metro 2039 now has a firm release date: **February 4, 2027** across its announced platforms, with some territories including Asia, Australia and New Zealand following on February 5.

The date arrived alongside the game’s first console gameplay, captured on PlayStation 5 Pro during Sony’s September State of Play. More importantly for players comparing console versions, Deep Silver and 4A Games have confirmed a **60fps Performance Mode with ray tracing** for PS5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X at launch.

Preorders are not open yet, but the game can already be wishlisted and 4A says preorders will begin later in 2026.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: A gas-masked soldier holding a rifle stands in a ruined snowy city beside the Metro 2039 logo.

contentBlocks.text: **Metro 2039 launches February 4, 2027**. Deep Silver notes that some territories, including Asia, Australia and New Zealand, will receive the game on **February 5**. The publisher says the February release applies across the game’s platforms, with preorders planned for later in 2026.
contentBlocks.heading: Metro 2039 release date

contentBlocks.text: 4A Games has confirmed a **60fps Performance Mode with ray tracing** for **PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X** at launch. The State of Play gameplay trailer itself was captured on PS5 Pro running in that 60fps Performance Mode. Deep Silver says more information about technology, specifications and the other available modes will be shared before release.
contentBlocks.heading: 60fps ray tracing is confirmed on PS5 and Xbox Series X

contentBlocks.text: According to 4A Games, Metro 2039 is the first entry in the series built from the ground up around ray tracing using the studio’s proprietary 4A Engine. That follows Metro Exodus Enhanced Edition, which previously used ray-traced lighting while targeting 60fps on current-generation consoles. The new game is intended to push that technology further rather than treating ray tracing as an optional late addition.
contentBlocks.heading: Metro 2039 is built around ray tracing from the start

contentBlocks.text: Metro 2039 can be wishlisted now, but **preorders are scheduled for later in 2026**. Deep Silver has not given the exact preorder date yet. The publisher is also taking registrations for information about a Collector’s Edition, but buyers who only want the standard game should wait for the formal preorder rollout rather than treating interest registration as an order.
contentBlocks.heading: When do Metro 2039 preorders open?

conclusion: Metro 2039’s State of Play appearance answered two of the biggest pre-launch questions at once: when it releases and whether console players can get 60fps without dropping ray tracing entirely. More platform-specific technical details are still coming, so this page should be updated as 4A Games publishes final mode and specification information.

newsMeta.sourceName: Deep Silver / Metro 2039 launches February 4th 2027

title: GTA 6 DualSense Controller Preorders: Price, Release Date and Where to Buy
description: GTA 6 DualSense preorders open September 10. Here are the black and white controller prices, release date, retailer availability and buying details.
body:
Sony has revealed two limited-edition DualSense wireless controllers inspired by Grand Theft Auto VI, giving players black and white designs built around Vice City’s neon-and-sunset visual identity.

Both controllers are scheduled to launch starting November 19, 2026, the same date currently listed for Grand Theft Auto VI on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The recommended price is $84.99 in the United States, €84.99 in Europe and £74.99 in the UK.

The more urgent detail is the preorder date: Sony says orders open September 10, with availability varying between the white and black editions and by region.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Black Grand Theft Auto VI limited-edition DualSense controller shown front-on against a purple and orange gradient background.

contentBlocks.text: Sony says preorders begin **September 10, 2026**. Through PlayStation Direct, ordering starts at **7:00am PT / 10:00am ET in the United States** and at **10:00am local time** in supported European PlayStation Direct markets. Quantities are limited, and Sony notes that exact availability can vary by country or region.
contentBlocks.heading: When do GTA 6 DualSense preorders open?

contentBlocks.text: Both the **Grand Theft Auto VI Black Limited Edition** and **Grand Theft Auto VI White Limited Edition** DualSense controllers have the same recommended retail price: **$84.99 / €84.99 / £74.99**. Sony says they will launch starting **November 19, 2026**. That date also matches Rockstar’s current console release date for GTA VI.
contentBlocks.heading: GTA 6 DualSense price and release date

contentBlocks.text: The white and black designs do not have identical distribution. Sony says the **white edition** will be sold in limited quantities through PlayStation Direct and participating retailers globally. The **black edition** is exclusive to PlayStation Direct in regions where that store operates, while other regions will receive it through select retailers. That makes the white controller the easier version to search for across standard retailers, while the black design may require PlayStation Direct in supported countries.
contentBlocks.heading: Where can you buy the black and white GTA 6 controllers?

contentBlocks.text: Both editions use a color-shifting finish inspired by Vice City’s daylight and nightlife palette, with molded palm-tree details and official Grand Theft Auto VI branding. The white model is built around a brighter coastal look, while the black controller leans into Vice City’s night-time neon aesthetic. They remain standard DualSense controllers, including adaptive triggers and haptic feedback supported by compatible PS5 games.
contentBlocks.heading: What is different about the GTA 6 design?

conclusion: For buyers, the key distinction is availability rather than features: both controllers share the same GTA VI theme, launch window and recommended price, but Sony is distributing the white edition more broadly. Neural Critic will update this page when preorder listings go live on September 10.

title: PS5 State of Play September 2026: GTA 6, FF7 Revelation and Every Announcement
description: Every major announcement from PlayStation’s September 2026 State of Play, including GTA 6 controllers, FF7 Revelation, Until Dawn 2, Metro 2039 and more.
body:
Sony’s September 2026 State of Play double-header is over, and the useful part now is separating the biggest announcements from the flood of trailers. The regular State of Play was followed immediately by State of Play Japan, with Sony saying the two broadcasts covered more than 30 games.

The headline reveals included an April 8, 2027 release date for Final Fantasy VII Revelation, a January 28, 2027 launch for Until Dawn 2, a February 4, 2027 date for Metro 2039, two limited-edition GTA 6 DualSense controllers, and a 1,911-piece LEGO replica of the original PlayStation.

Below is Neural Critic’s fast, search-friendly recap of the games, dates, demos, expansions and hardware announcements worth knowing from the September 3 showcase.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Split promotional graphic for PlayStation State of Play and State of Play Japan.

contentBlocks.text:
**Final Fantasy VII Revelation** finally has a date: April 8, 2027. Square Enix also detailed new traversal and combat systems, physical and digital editions, 24-hour early access in premium digital packages, and a Story Expansion Pass.

**Until Dawn 2** launches January 28, 2027 on PS5, with preorders opening September 10. Firesprite also outlined its Digital Deluxe Edition and preorder bonuses.

**Metro 2039** launches February 4, 2027. 4A Games used State of Play to debut console gameplay captured on PS5 Pro and confirmed a 60fps Performance Mode with ray tracing for PS5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X.

**Grand Theft Auto VI** did not receive a new game trailer, but Sony revealed black and white limited-edition GTA VI DualSense controllers. Preorders open September 10 and both designs begin launching November 19.

**LEGO PlayStation** recreates the original PlayStation console and controller in a 1,911-piece near-1:1-scale set, with PlayStation and LEGO availability beginning in October.
contentBlocks.heading: The five biggest State of Play announcements

contentBlocks.text:
Sony’s official recap includes more than 30 game and service updates. The major announcements were:

- **CONQ: Crown of No Quarter** — new shared-open-world warfare game revealed.
- **Crimson Desert: Charting the Unknown** — expansion dated for October 15.
- **Daba: Land of Water Scar** — coming to PS5 in spring 2027.
- **Digimon Story Time Stranger: A Hero’s Eternal Legacy** — story expansion coming in 2027.
- **Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3** — coming to PS5 in 2027.
- **Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World** — launches December 3 on PS5.
- **Echoes of Aincrad: Sword Art Online – Genesis Maidens** — first DLC arriving this winter.
- **Fate/Extra Record** — launches January 28, 2027 on PS5 and PS4.
- **Final Fantasy Resonance** — October 22 release reinforced, with a demo available now and Sephiroth revealed as a challenge.
- **Final Fantasy VII Revelation** — launches April 8, 2027.
- **Ghost of Yōtei** — Most Wanted survival mode and Echoes of Sekigahara content arrive with the Complete Edition on October 1.
- **Gran Turismo 7** — Spec IV update split across October and December with new circuits, cars and modes.
- **GTA VI Limited Edition DualSense controllers** — black and white designs launch starting November 19, with preorders September 10.
- **Gundam Rogue Orbit** — launches March 5, 2027.
- **Hunter’s Moon** — historical folk-horror coming to PS5 in October.
- **Keeper** — Double Fine’s puzzle adventure is available on PS5 now.
- **LEGO PlayStation** — original-console replica launches in October.
- **Maneater 2** — sequel announced for PS5 in 2027.
- **Marvel’s Wolverine** — launch trailer shown ahead of its September 15, 2026 release.
- **Metro 2039** — launches February 4, 2027.
- **Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance** — major expansion coming in 2027.
- **PlayStation Plus** — Mycopunk joins Game Catalog, while Mega Man X: Command Mission, Dino Crisis 2 and the original Ratchet & Clank are headed to Premium Classics.
- **Rematch x Blue Lock** — collaboration launches September 24.
- **Resident Evil** — new look at Zach Cregger’s film adaptation ahead of its September cinema release.
- **Rev. Noir** — new gameplay shown and a 2027 window confirmed.
- **Rhapsody in Scarlet** — new Konami action-adventure revealed.
- **Saros Zenith** — free update adds boss-rush and New Game Plus-style content later this year.
- **SlashZero** — PS5 demo available now; full game planned for spring 2027.
- **Stupid Never Dies** — demo available now, with save transfer into the October 21 launch.
- **The Eminence in Shadow: Phantom Echoes** — first console game in the series, coming to PS5 in 2027.
- **Uncanyon** — reality-bending puzzle adventure from Graceful Decay coming to PS5 in 2027.
- **Until Dawn 2** — launches January 28, 2027.
- **Where the Seeds Fall** — launches November 5, 2026 on PS5.
- **World Phasebound Control Authority: WPCA** — supernatural action RPG coming to PS5 in 2028.
contentBlocks.heading: Every major announcement from State of Play and State of Play Japan

contentBlocks.text: The showcase produced several dates that players are likely to search repeatedly over the next few months. Marvel’s Wolverine is due September 15, 2026; Where the Seeds Fall follows November 5; the GTA VI DualSense controllers and GTA VI itself are set for November 19; Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World arrives December 3; Fate/Extra Record and Until Dawn 2 both land January 28, 2027; Metro 2039 follows February 4; Gundam Rogue Orbit arrives March 5; and Final Fantasy VII Revelation closes the current run of major dates on April 8, 2027.
contentBlocks.heading: The release dates worth saving

contentBlocks.text: A giant recap is useful for the broad State of Play query, but the most actionable searches are more specific: GTA 6 controller preorder details, LEGO PlayStation price and release date, Final Fantasy VII Revelation platforms and editions, Until Dawn 2 preorders, and Metro 2039’s 60fps ray-tracing mode. Those stories are being covered separately so this recap can act as the hub rather than trying to answer every question in one page.
contentBlocks.heading: Neural Critic is breaking out the highest-intent searches

conclusion: The September showcase was less about one surprise megaton than about firming up Sony’s late-2026 and early-2027 calendar. The strongest search opportunities are the announcements with concrete dates, prices and preorder information, which Neural Critic is covering separately and linking back into this recap.

title: LEGO PlayStation Price, Release Date and 1,911-Piece Set Details
description: The 1,911-piece LEGO PlayStation recreates Sony’s original console and controller. Here are the price, October release dates and availability details.
body:
Sony and the LEGO Group have turned the original PlayStation into a 1,911-piece display set that recreates both the console and its controller at close to real-world scale.

The LEGO PlayStation launches first on October 1, 2026 through PlayStation Direct in supported markets and through LEGO Insiders Early Access. Wider LEGO.com and LEGO Store availability begins October 4.

The recommended price is $179.99 in the US, €159.99 in Europe and £139.99 in the UK.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: LEGO model of the original gray PlayStation console with a wired LEGO controller on a wooden table.

contentBlocks.text: Sony lists the LEGO PlayStation at **$179.99 / €159.99 / £139.99 / ¥27,980**. It becomes available through **PlayStation Direct on October 1, 2026** in supported markets. LEGO Insiders also get Early Access on October 1, while broader availability through LEGO.com and LEGO Stores begins **October 4**.
contentBlocks.heading: LEGO PlayStation price and release date

contentBlocks.text: The set uses **1,911 pieces** and is designed as a near-1:1-scale recreation of the original PlayStation console. Sony says the completed model measures **10.5 inches / 26 cm wide**. The build also includes a LEGO version of the original PlayStation controller that can connect to the console model.
contentBlocks.heading: How big is the LEGO PlayStation set?

contentBlocks.text: The model is not only an exterior shell. Sony and LEGO included references to two games associated with the original PlayStation era: **Ape Escape** and **Gran Turismo**. Each gets a small removable diorama, with the Gran Turismo display featuring a miniature track and cars while the Ape Escape scene includes a small island setup. The console’s Power and Open buttons also have functional mechanisms.
contentBlocks.heading: Ape Escape and Gran Turismo are hidden inside the nostalgia

contentBlocks.text: PlayStation Direct availability on October 1 covers supported markets including the US, UK and several European countries. LEGO Insiders can access the set from the same date, while the general LEGO retail window starts October 4. That means buyers who do not use PlayStation Direct or LEGO Insiders should treat October 4 as the broad release date.
contentBlocks.heading: Where will LEGO PlayStation be sold?

conclusion: The LEGO PlayStation is unusually easy to understand as a product: it is a large display-focused recreation of Sony’s first console with functional details and two small game-history dioramas. The main buying questions are price, October availability and whether buyers need LEGO Insiders access for the earliest window.

newsMeta.sourceName: PlayStation Blog / LEGO PlayStation first look

title: Until Dawn 2 Release Date, Preorders and Digital Deluxe Edition Explained
description: Until Dawn 2 launches January 28, 2027 on PS5. Here are the preorder date, Digital Deluxe Edition details and key State of Play reveals.
body:
Until Dawn 2 has moved from a broad 2027 window to a firm **January 28, 2027** release date on PlayStation 5.

Firesprite used Sony’s September State of Play to confirm the date, reveal that preorders open September 10, and detail both preorder bonuses and a Digital Deluxe Edition.

The sequel is a standalone choice-driven horror story following the paranormal-video crew Dead True as they investigate Akishima Island, with AdHoc Studio working with Firesprite on the narrative.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: A translucent skeletal apparition glows green and orange in a dark, rain-soaked forest scene from Until Dawn 2.

contentBlocks.text: **Until Dawn 2 launches January 28, 2027 on PlayStation 5.** Sony and Firesprite have not announced PS4, Xbox, Nintendo Switch 2 or PC versions. The sequel is designed as a standalone story rather than a direct continuation that requires players to know every outcome from the original Until Dawn.
contentBlocks.heading: Until Dawn 2 release date and platform

contentBlocks.text: Preorders open **September 10, 2026** for both the Standard and Digital Deluxe Editions. Sony says preordering either version unlocks a group of Dr. Hill-themed bonuses, including two outfits and collectible Dr. Hill bobbleheads that can be found in the game.
contentBlocks.heading: When do Until Dawn 2 preorders open?

contentBlocks.text: The Digital Deluxe Edition adds the **Y2K Neon Vibes Pack**, which gives the eight members of Dead True alternate neon outfits, plus a feature called **Diorama of Death** that lets players revisit unlocked character-outcome scenes from different angles. Sony has not yet published pricing in the announcement, so the safest comparison for now is based on content rather than cost.
contentBlocks.heading: What is in the Digital Deluxe Edition?

contentBlocks.text: The new cast belongs to **Dead True**, a paranormal-video team whose investigation takes them to Akishima Island. Firesprite says the story keeps the series’ defining choice-and-consequence structure, where decisions affect relationships, clues and who makes it through the story. AdHoc Studio, known for Dispatch, is collaborating on the narrative and character writing, while Peter Stormare returns as Dr. Hill.
contentBlocks.heading: What is Until Dawn 2 about?

conclusion: Until Dawn 2 now has the three details players are most likely to search before launch: a date, a preorder window and clear edition differences. Firesprite still has months to reveal more about the story and gameplay, but the January launch plan is now concrete.

newsMeta.sourceName: PlayStation Blog / Until Dawn 2 launches January 28

title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation Release Date, Platforms, Editions and Early Access
description: Final Fantasy VII Revelation launches April 8, 2027. Here are the confirmed platforms, editions, preorder bonuses and 24-hour early-access details.
body:
Final Fantasy VII Revelation now has a firm release date. Square Enix says the conclusion to the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy launches **April 8, 2027** across PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S and PC.

The announcement also turns Revelation into a much clearer buying decision. Physical and digital preorders are opening across platforms, Square Enix has outlined multiple editions, and its premium digital packages include a Story Expansion Pass plus 24-hour early access.

That makes this State of Play update more useful as a release-and-editions reference than as another trailer recap.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Cloud Strife kneels among yellow flowers with party members standing behind him in a luminous ruined environment.

contentBlocks.text: **Final Fantasy VII Revelation launches April 8, 2027** on **PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S and PC**. On PC, Square Enix lists Steam, Epic Games Store and Xbox on PC. Square Enix describes this as the conclusion to the three-part remake project and says the game will release across those platforms on the same date.
contentBlocks.heading: Final Fantasy VII Revelation release date and platforms

contentBlocks.text: Square Enix has confirmed multiple physical and digital options. In the US, the physical lineup includes a **Standard Edition at $69.99**, a **Deluxe Edition at $99.99**, and a **$349.99 Collector’s Edition** sold through the Square Enix Store. The Deluxe package adds physical extras such as an art book, mini soundtrack and SteelBook, while the Collector’s Edition expands further with additional premium contents. Digital availability includes premium tiers aimed at players who want DLC and early access rather than physical collectibles.
contentBlocks.heading: What editions are available?

contentBlocks.text: Square Enix says the digital **Premium Edition** includes the main game, a **Story Expansion Pass** and **24-hour early access**, allowing owners to begin playing one day before the standard release. A **Premium Plus Edition** adds further digital extras. The Story Expansion Pass is planned to include two story-focused DLC releases, with Square Enix identifying Sephiroth and Vincent & the Turks as the focus of those expansions.
contentBlocks.heading: How does 24-hour early access work?

contentBlocks.text: Physical and digital preorders are opening across the announced platforms, although Square Enix notes that digital Nintendo Switch 2 preorders will open later. The company is also offering save-data bonuses for players with Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade and/or Final Fantasy VII Rebirth data on the same console or PC ecosystem, giving returning players additional summon materia and weapon-skin rewards in Revelation.
contentBlocks.heading: Preorders and save-data bonuses

contentBlocks.text: The release-date announcement came with a deeper gameplay presentation built around large-scale traversal and party flexibility. Players can travel aboard the Highwind, use chocobos as both mounts and combat partners, swap party members dynamically while exploring, and use the new FITS system to alter combat roles and move sets. Square Enix also says some quests can be assigned to different party members, changing how specific scenarios play out.
contentBlocks.heading: What State of Play revealed about gameplay

conclusion: The most important change is that Revelation is no longer just a spring-2027 release. It now has one worldwide date across its announced platforms, and Square Enix has put enough edition information on the table for players to compare what they actually receive before preordering.

newsMeta.sourceName: Square Enix / Final Fantasy VII Revelation release-date announcement

title: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet Wraps ‘Very Ambitious’ Cinematic Shoot
description: Naughty Dog has wrapped Intergalactic’s cinematic shoot, marking a major PS5 development milestone. A September 3 State of Play is confirmed, but the game is not.
body:
Naughty Dog has completed the cinematic shoot for Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, giving the studio’s new PS5 franchise its clearest public development milestone in months.

In an August 31 social post, Naughty Dog described the shoot as “very ambitious” and said it was eager to show the cast’s work “when the time is right.” The announcement was accompanied by a new production image of lead actor Tati Gabrielle, who plays bounty hunter Jordan A. Mun.

The timing will inevitably fuel speculation about Sony’s September 3 State of Play, but PlayStation has not announced Intergalactic for the presentation. The game also still has no confirmed release date.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Jordan A. Mun stands in official Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet key art against a science-fiction backdrop.
imageCredit: Sony Interactive Entertainment / Naughty Dog — official Intergalactic artwork

contentBlocks.text: Wrapping the cinematic shoot is a meaningful production milestone, but it does not mean Intergalactic itself is finished. Naughty Dog has not announced how much gameplay, animation, engineering or post-production work remains, and the studio did not attach a release window to the update. The safest reading is therefore the simplest one: the cast-led cinematic work has reached an important endpoint while the wider game remains in development.
contentBlocks.heading: A major production milestone, not a release-date announcement

contentBlocks.text: Tati Gabrielle plays Jordan A. Mun, the bounty hunter at the center of Intergalactic. Naughty Dog’s original announcement says Jordan becomes stranded on Sempiria, a distant planet cut off from the wider universe, and must try to become the first person in more than 600 years to leave its orbit. The studio has said the PS5 project has been in development since 2020.
contentBlocks.heading: Tati Gabrielle remains at the center of Naughty Dog’s new franchise

contentBlocks.text: The shoot-wrap follows another recent cast update. On August 21, veteran performer Robin Atkin Downes publicly confirmed that he is working on Intergalactic and said he was happy to be collaborating with Naughty Dog again. His role has not been revealed, so any attempt to identify his character would be speculation.
contentBlocks.heading: Robin Atkin Downes recently added another confirmed cast name

contentBlocks.text: Sony has announced a State of Play for September 3 featuring updates from PlayStation Studios and third-party partners. Intergalactic was not named in PlayStation’s announcement. The close timing between that showcase and Naughty Dog’s production update makes a new appearance an obvious possibility for fans to discuss, but there is currently no official confirmation that the game will be shown.
contentBlocks.heading: State of Play is confirmed — Intergalactic is not

contentBlocks.text: PlayStation’s current game page lists Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet for PS5 with its release date still to be confirmed. Reports and community speculation around a possible 2027 launch should therefore remain separate from the confirmed record until Sony or Naughty Dog announces a window.
contentBlocks.heading: Intergalactic still has no confirmed release date

conclusion: ==For now, the meaningful news is straightforward: Intergalactic has completed its ambitious cinematic shoot, Naughty Dog is publicly marking progress again, and the cast picture continues to expand. Anything beyond that — including a September 3 appearance or a specific release window — remains unconfirmed.==

updates.note: Robin Atkin Downes publicly confirmed that he is working on Intergalactic; his role remains undisclosed.
PlayStation announced a September 3 State of Play but did not name Intergalactic among the confirmed games.

newsMeta.sourceName: Naughty Dog official social post / GamesRadar

title: EXODUS Gameplay Deep Dive Reveals Salt, Combat and a Time-Dilated Sci-Fi RPG
description: Game Informer’s new EXODUS deep dive follows a four-hour hands-on session at Archetype Entertainment, revealing more about Salt, combat, the Awakened and the RPG’s time-dilation story.
body: EXODUS has already shown its release date and broad RPG structure, but a new hands-on deep dive from Game Informer gives a much clearer sense of how Archetype Entertainment’s sci-fi RPG plays and how its biggest narrative idea — time dilation — affects the world around protagonist Jun Aslan. Game Informer visited Archetype’s Austin studio and played roughly four hours of the game, with its latest discussion focusing on combat, lore, companions and one of EXODUS’ most unusual Awakened characters: Salt, an intelligent octopus who operates from inside a heavily armed mech. The new material expands on systems Archetype previously introduced without replacing the core pitch: Jun is a salvager turned Traveler crossing the Centauri Cluster, assembling a crew and making decisions that can reshape the people and societies left behind.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: A Traveller walks through a dark alien cavern toward companions and a hovering drone beneath the glowing face of a Celestial figure.
imageCredit: Archetype Entertainment / Wizards of the Coast

contentBlocks.text: The latest EXODUS coverage comes from a studio visit rather than another trailer. Game Informer says its editors traveled to Archetype Entertainment in Austin and played roughly four hours of the game before discussing the experience in a new story and gameplay deep dive. That makes the coverage useful as a hands-on follow-up to the material Archetype has already released publicly. The session included combat, exploration and time spent with companions, while also giving the publication more context on the setting and the people Jun meets across the Centauri Cluster.
contentBlocks.heading: Game Informer played around four hours of EXODUS

contentBlocks.text: Salt is one of EXODUS’ Awakened — intelligent animals that live alongside humans in the game’s far-future society. Archetype’s release-date trailer introduced her as a mercenary and bounty hunter, but the new deep dive spends more time on what makes her memorable: she is an octopus operating from inside a railgun-equipped mech and can become part of Jun’s crew. Archetype has said companions can include both humans and Awakened animals, each with their own history, skills and reasons for joining the mission.
contentBlocks.heading: Salt is more than the strange octopus in the trailer

contentBlocks.text: Salt is not an isolated novelty. Archetype narrative director Drew Karpyshyn has described the Awakened as one of the defining ideas of the EXODUS universe, alongside time dilation. Game Informer’s hands-on coverage also describes the Kay, a society of giant intelligent frogs encountered at the Khonsu space station. These characters help establish that the game’s far future is not simply built around humans and conventional alien factions; evolution and engineered intelligence have produced societies that can be physically and culturally very different from Jun’s own.
contentBlocks.heading: The Awakened make EXODUS’ universe stranger than a standard space opera

contentBlocks.text: Archetype’s earlier extended gameplay reveal established the foundation: third-person combat across hostile worlds, exploration of fallen civilizations, human and Awakened companions, and decisions that shape Jun’s path. The studio has also shown Paladin and Immortal morality alignments that influence who Jun becomes. The new Game Informer material adds hands-on context to those systems rather than presenting a completely different game. EXODUS is still being positioned as a story-heavy action RPG where shooting and exploration sit alongside companion relationships, moral decisions and long-term consequences.
contentBlocks.heading: Combat sits inside a much larger choice-driven RPG structure

contentBlocks.text: EXODUS is set roughly 40,000 years in the future, and Archetype is treating relativity as more than background lore. Travelers such as Jun can cross interstellar distances, but the people and societies they leave behind continue aging while far less time passes for the Traveler. Archetype has repeatedly framed that difference as a source of emotional and political consequences: returning from a mission can mean discovering that years or decades have passed elsewhere. That gives the game a built-in way to make major choices echo beyond the immediate mission and helps distinguish its story structure from a conventional planet-hopping RPG.
contentBlocks.heading: Time dilation is still EXODUS’ most important narrative mechanic

contentBlocks.text: Archetype Entertainment has confirmed that EXODUS launches on April 7, 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC. Neural Critic previously covered the [EXODUS April 7, 2027 release-date announcement](/stories/exodus-release-date-april-7-2027-gamescom/) from Opening Night Live. The newer hands-on coverage is valuable for a different reason: it moves the conversation beyond when EXODUS is coming out and toward how its combat, companions and time-dilated universe actually fit together. With Game Informer now having played several hours, EXODUS is beginning to look less like an ambitious pitch and more like a playable RPG whose unusual ideas can be judged on their implementation.
contentBlocks.heading: EXODUS launches April 7, 2027

newsMeta.sourceName: Game Informer / Exclusive EXODUS Story And Gameplay Deep Dive

title: Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis Gameplay Reimagines Peru, Puzzles and the T-Rex
description: An extended gamescom 2026 gameplay presentation for Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis shows Lara exploring Peru, solving rebuilt puzzles and facing raptors and a reimagined T-Rex.
body: Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis received an extended gameplay showcase at gamescom 2026, offering one of the clearest looks yet at how Crystal Dynamics and Flying Wild Hog are rebuilding Lara Croft’s original adventure. The demonstration focuses on Peru’s Lost Valley, moving from exploration and puzzle-solving into combat against raptors and the series’ iconic T-Rex encounter. Rather than recreating the 1996 game room for room, the developers continue to describe Legacy of Atlantis as a reimagining: recognizable locations and ideas return, but traversal, puzzles and combat have been rebuilt around a modern third-person action-adventure structure.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Lara Croft stands overlooking a misty valley filled with jungle vegetation, rocky peaks and ancient ruins.
imageCredit: Crystal Dynamics / Flying Wild Hog / Amazon Game Studios

contentBlocks.text: The extended presentation takes place in Peru, revisiting the Lost Valley and the route toward the Tomb of Qualopec. It shows Lara moving through a much larger, more connected version of the location rather than a sequence of isolated rooms. That approach matches Crystal Dynamics’ earlier explanation of the project: Legacy of Atlantis keeps the identity of the original adventure while expanding its environments so exploration can support more routes, verticality and environmental storytelling. The footage also reinforces the brighter visual direction of this reimagining, with dense jungle, ancient ruins and wide environmental vistas replacing the more abstract spaces of the 1996 original.
contentBlocks.heading: The gamescom demo returns to Peru’s Lost Valley

contentBlocks.text: One of the showcase’s clearest examples of the reimagining philosophy is the familiar cog puzzle near the Tomb of Qualopec. Lara still needs to restore an ancient mechanism, but the surrounding spaces have been opened up and the puzzle has been given a stronger in-world purpose. Instead of simply finding objects in disconnected rooms, the player explores the ruins, reads environmental clues and works out how the mechanism fits into the location itself. Crystal Dynamics has repeatedly said it wants Legacy of Atlantis to preserve Tomb Raider’s emphasis on observation and discovery without reducing exploration to constant waypoints or obvious directions.
contentBlocks.heading: The classic cog puzzle has been rebuilt around the environment

contentBlocks.text: Lara’s movement remains central to the demo. She climbs, jumps and crosses the ruins using the kind of athletic traversal associated with Tomb Raider, while the reimagining adds modern tools and more contextual movement. The gamescom footage also shows a grappling tool being used to cross gaps and interact with the environment. The goal appears to be a middle ground between the precision and acrobatic identity of classic Tomb Raider and the smoother movement systems developed across the Survivor trilogy.
contentBlocks.heading: Traversal mixes classic acrobatics with a more modern toolkit

contentBlocks.text: The second half of the presentation shifts into combat as Lara encounters raptors and, eventually, the T-Rex. Legacy of Atlantis keeps her dual pistols but builds the combat around constant movement rather than cover. Crystal Dynamics describes the game as a modern third-person shooter where Lara’s agility is part of the combat loop: dodges, acrobatic movement and aggressive positioning are meant to keep her mobile while she fires. The game also uses a Focus system that can slow time during combat, giving Lara room to turn her acrobatics into offensive opportunities. The T-Rex encounter is not being reproduced exactly as it appeared in 1996; the developers have described it as a larger, more cinematic reimagining of one of Tomb Raider’s most recognizable moments.
contentBlocks.heading: Raptors and the T-Rex show how combat has changed

contentBlocks.text: The gamescom demonstration makes the developers’ terminology especially important. Crystal Dynamics and Flying Wild Hog are not presenting Legacy of Atlantis as a scene-for-scene remake. The original Tomb Raider remains the foundation, but the teams are changing the scale of environments, rebuilding puzzles, expanding combat and drawing on ideas from later Tomb Raider games. At the same time, this version of Lara is intended to continue the character established by the Survivor trilogy rather than exist as a disconnected interpretation. That gives the project an unusual role: it returns to Lara’s first adventure while also moving the current version of the character forward.
contentBlocks.heading: Legacy of Atlantis is a reimagining, not a scene-for-scene remake

contentBlocks.text: Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis is scheduled to launch on February 12, 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, PC via Steam and Nintendo Switch 2. Crystal Dynamics is co-developing the game with Flying Wild Hog, with Amazon Game Studios publishing. The extended gamescom footage does not reveal the full scope of the reimagining, but it gives a much stronger sense of how the developers are balancing the structure of the original with modern traversal, combat and environmental design.
contentBlocks.heading: Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis launches in February 2027

newsMeta.sourceName: Xbox / Crystal Dynamics / Flying Wild Hog

title: Fable’s 18-Minute Gameplay Shows Bowerstone, Property Ownership and Choice
description: Playground Games has released 18 minutes of Fable gameplay from gamescom 2026, showing a quest through Bowerstone, property ownership, choice and consequence, and combat.
body: Playground Games has released 18 minutes of new Fable gameplay from gamescom 2026, giving players one of the clearest looks yet at how Albion’s reimagined capital, Bowerstone, works in practice. The footage follows a full quest through the city and puts several of Fable’s core ideas on display at once: exploration, property ownership, character interaction, choice and consequence, and combat. It also introduces Humphry, the disgraced leader of the Heroes’ Guild, as part of the quest. Fable is scheduled to launch February 23, 2027.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: The Fable hero stands in a glowing forest clearing, looking toward a distant castle beneath the game’s logo.
imageCredit: Playground Games / Xbox Game Studios

contentBlocks.text: Xbox has published the full 18-minute quest demonstration that Playground Games showed at gamescom 2026. Rather than cutting quickly between isolated mechanics, the footage follows the Hero through Bowerstone and gives the city room to function as a place rather than just a backdrop. The demonstration shows streets, interiors, conversations and quest progression while introducing Humphry, the disgraced leader of the Heroes’ Guild. It is a much more useful look at how Fable’s world fits together moment to moment than a conventional trailer.
contentBlocks.heading: The new footage spends 18 minutes inside Bowerstone

contentBlocks.text: One of the most striking details highlighted by Playground Games is the degree of access players have to Bowerstone. Xbox says every building in the city can be entered and every house can be purchased. That puts property ownership back near the center of Fable’s life-simulation side, rather than treating the city as a collection of decorative storefronts. The footage reinforces Playground’s broader pitch for a living Albion where the Hero can build a life outside the main quest instead of simply passing through settlements between combat encounters.
contentBlocks.heading: Every building can be entered — and every house can be bought

contentBlocks.text: The Bowerstone quest also demonstrates Fable’s familiar emphasis on player decisions. Xbox specifically points to choice and consequence as one of the systems shown during the walkthrough, tying individual actions to the wider reputation system Playground Games has been describing for the reboot. The studio’s official material says a Hero’s noble deeds and questionable decisions can affect relationships with individual villagers and can shape the world around them. The new quest footage is useful because it shows those ideas inside ordinary play rather than presenting them only as a high-level feature list.
contentBlocks.heading: Choice and consequence are built into the quest

contentBlocks.text: The extended gameplay includes multiple combat encounters, building on the playable gamescom demo Playground Games previously used to explain Fable’s combat system. The reboot evolves the original trilogy’s Strength, Skill and Will framework by letting players move between melee weapons, ranged attacks and magic during the same fight. Equipment and unlocked skills can change how those options work together, but the basic idea is flexibility: the Hero is not locked into one combat discipline when a situation changes.
contentBlocks.heading: Combat mixes melee, ranged attacks and magic

contentBlocks.text: Fable is scheduled to launch on February 23, 2027. Xbox lists Xbox Series X|S, Xbox on PC, cloud play and Game Pass support, with Xbox Play Anywhere between console and PC. PlayStation also lists a PlayStation 5 version for the same February 23 release date, marking the series’ first appearance on PS5. The Premium Edition includes early access beginning February 18. With the release date now set, the gamescom footage shifts the conversation from what Playground’s reboot is trying to be toward how its systems actually feel when they are allowed to run together across a full quest.
contentBlocks.heading: Fable launches in February 2027

title: The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past Gameplay Shows Letten and Geralt’s New Chain
description: New Songs of the Past gameplay takes Geralt through Letten, shows an early quest, and demonstrates the Witcher 3 expansion’s new silver chain combat.
body: CD Projekt Red has released a longer public gameplay look at The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Songs of the Past, giving players a clearer sense of how Geralt’s return to the Path will actually play. The footage moves through Letten, an entirely new open-world region, and shows exploration, questing, combat and one of the expansion’s most noticeable mechanical additions: Geralt’s silver chain.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Geralt rides Roach toward a large timber-built settlement in Letten, surrounded by stone walls, trees and wildflowers.
imageCredit: CD PROJEKT RED / Fool’s Theory

contentBlocks.text:
Songs of the Past takes Geralt to **Letten**, a new open-world region that CD Projekt Red describes as idyllic on the surface but hiding something sinister underneath. The longer gameplay showcase makes that contrast much easier to see. Geralt travels through pastoral countryside and lived-in settlements before the journey turns toward darker woodland and thorn-covered spaces.

Letten is presented as a region with its own identity rather than an extension of Velen or Toussaint. Reporting from the gameplay showcase says the area draws on rural Polish and English influences, with local customs, architecture and a landscape relatively untouched by war. The result is a setting that looks peaceful enough to invite exploration while still fitting The Witcher 3’s habit of placing unsettling stories behind picturesque scenery.

CD Projekt Red has confirmed that Letten brings new quests, characters, locations and secrets, with Songs of the Past scheduled for 2027.
contentBlocks.heading: The new footage gives us a proper look at Letten

contentBlocks.text:
The gameplay follows part of an early quest called **A Bed of Thorns**, giving us a better sense of how the expansion moves between exploration, conversation, investigation and combat.

Rather than functioning as a detached combat demonstration, the sequence is built around Geralt following a trail through Letten and gradually moving toward a more threatening environment. That familiar rhythm matters because it suggests Songs of the Past is extending The Witcher 3’s established quest design instead of treating the expansion as a separate action showcase.

The expansion is also tied closely to Dandelion and his homeland. CD Projekt Red has positioned Letten as a place connected to the bard’s past, giving the new region a personal narrative reason to exist rather than simply adding another map for Geralt to explore.
contentBlocks.heading: An early quest shows how Songs of the Past is structured

contentBlocks.text:
The most obvious mechanical addition shown in the new footage is Geralt’s **silver chain**. The showcase demonstrates it as another way to control space during combat, letting Geralt interfere with enemies and create openings before following up with his familiar swords and Signs.

The chain does not appear to replace The Witcher 3’s existing combat system. Instead, it expands Geralt’s toolkit while keeping the core loop recognizable: positioning, sword attacks, Signs and preparation still sit at the center of encounters.

That makes the addition more interesting than a purely cosmetic callback. It gives returning players something new to experiment with while preserving the combat language of the original game.
contentBlocks.heading: Geralt’s silver chain adds a new combat option

contentBlocks.text:
The gameplay remains immediately recognizable as The Witcher 3. Geralt explores an open environment, speaks with characters, investigates clues and gets pulled into combat when the trail turns dangerous.

At the same time, Songs of the Past is arriving alongside the remastered version of The Witcher 3, and the presentation reflects a broader effort to modernize the game’s feel and presentation for current hardware. That context is important: the expansion is not being built as though the 2015 version of The Witcher 3 has remained untouched for more than a decade.

For returning players, that combination may be one of the expansion’s biggest strengths. Songs of the Past can preserve the structure and tone people remember while benefiting from work designed to make The Witcher 3 feel less dated in 2026 and beyond.
contentBlocks.heading: Songs of the Past still feels like The Witcher 3 — just more modern

contentBlocks.text:
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Songs of the Past is scheduled for **2027** on **PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and Nintendo Switch 2**. CD Projekt Red and Fool’s Theory are developing the expansion together.

Our [original Songs of the Past reveal](/stories/witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-gamescom-2026-reveal/) established Letten and Geralt’s reason for returning. This longer gameplay showcase is more useful because it shows what that return actually looks like: a new region built around exploration and investigation, familiar Witcher quest structure, new monsters and a combat tool that meaningfully expands Geralt’s options.

CD Projekt Red has not announced a more specific release date. Until then, Songs of the Past already looks less like a nostalgic epilogue and more like a substantial new chapter built on the systems that made The Witcher 3 work in the first place.
contentBlocks.heading: Geralt returns to the Path in 2027

title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: Best Kart Builds and What the Stats Actually Mean
description: A practical breakdown of speed, acceleration, mini-turbo, handling, weight, and strong kart combinations for different Mario Kart 8 Deluxe playstyles.
body:
Mario Kart 8 Deluxe makes kart building look simple because the selection screen shows only a handful of stat bars. Underneath those bars, however, each driver, body, tire set, and glider contributes to several values, including a hidden Mini-Turbo stat that has a major effect on how a build feels in real races.

That is why the fastest-looking combination is rarely the best all-purpose choice. Strong builds usually balance enough speed with acceleration, handling, and Mini-Turbo so they can recover from items, hold clean lines, and generate useful boosts through repeated drifts. The current game version is 3.0.5, and the major balance changes that reshaped common builds arrived earlier, so the combinations below are based on the modern stat environment rather than the launch-era meta.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Mario drives a red kart beside the Mario Kart 8 Deluxe logo against a purple and pink gradient background.
imageCredit: Nintendo / Mario Kart 8 Deluxe promotional artwork.

contentBlocks.text:
Mario Kart 8 Deluxe rewards different strengths depending on the track, race format, and how consistently you can drift. A build with excellent top speed may look dominant on paper but lose time every time it is hit, forced into a tight corner, or asked to accelerate again.

That is why the strongest general-purpose combinations tend to avoid extreme weaknesses. They keep enough speed to stay competitive while preserving acceleration, handling, and Mini-Turbo.

Treat the recommended builds in this guide as starting points, not rules. If two setups are close statistically, the one you control more cleanly will usually be the better choice for you.
contentBlocks.caption: Strong Mario Kart 8 Deluxe builds balance several stats instead of maximizing a single number.
contentBlocks.heading: There Is No Single Best Kart Build for Every Player
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe vehicle customization screen showing a complete character, kart, tire, and glider setup with the stat bars visible.

contentBlocks.text:
Speed determines how fast your kart can travel once it is fully up to pace, but Mario Kart races are constantly interrupting that ideal situation. Items, off-road sections, collisions, jumps, corners, and mistakes all create moments where raw top speed matters less than how quickly you can return to it.

The game also tracks speed separately across ground, water, air, and anti-gravity sections, even though the selection screen compresses that information into a simpler display.

High speed is still valuable, especially on courses with long straights, but choosing a build only because its visible speed bar is large usually creates unnecessary weaknesses elsewhere.
contentBlocks.caption: Top speed matters most when a kart has enough time to stay at full pace, but races constantly interrupt that ideal situation.
contentBlocks.heading: Speed Matters, but It Does Not Tell the Whole Story
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe vehicle selection screen showing a speed-focused kart setup and its stat bars.

contentBlocks.text:
Acceleration controls how quickly you regain speed after slowing down. That makes it especially useful in ordinary online races, where shells, bananas, bumps, and crowded corners repeatedly interrupt your momentum.

A high-acceleration build is not automatically faster over an entire lap, but it is more forgiving when the race becomes messy. Newer players often benefit from that consistency because a single mistake costs less time.

Acceleration also pairs naturally with builds that emphasize Mini-Turbo and handling, creating setups that feel responsive rather than heavy.
contentBlocks.caption: Higher acceleration helps a kart recover more quickly after item hits, collisions, and other interruptions.
contentBlocks.heading: Acceleration Is Your Recovery Stat
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe vehicle selection screen showing an acceleration-focused setup with the stat bars visible.

contentBlocks.text:
Mini-Turbo does not appear as its own bar on the normal vehicle-selection screen, but it influences one of the most important techniques in the game: the boosts earned from drifting.

A stronger Mini-Turbo stat helps you charge drift boosts more effectively and improves the value you get from repeatedly taking clean corners. Because so many Mario Kart 8 Deluxe tracks are built around frequent drifting, that advantage can matter across an entire race rather than only on one straight.

This is one reason Roller and Azure Roller tires remain so useful. They sacrifice some raw speed but contribute strong acceleration, handling, and Mini-Turbo characteristics that work well with many competitive combinations.
contentBlocks.caption: Mini-Turbo is hidden from the normal stat display, but repeated drift boosts make it one of the most important performance stats.
contentBlocks.heading: Mini-Turbo Is the Hidden Stat You Should Not Ignore
contentBlocks.imageAlt: A racer drifts through a corner in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe with Mini-Turbo sparks glowing from the wheels.

contentBlocks.text:
Handling affects how sharply a vehicle can turn, while traction influences grip on slippery or loose surfaces. These stats rarely get the attention that speed receives, but they can determine how consistently you hold a racing line.

A build with better handling gives you more room to correct a drift that started too early or too late. That is especially valuable on technical courses with repeated bends.

Do not dismiss a slightly slower setup if it lets you take corners cleanly every lap. Consistency is a real performance advantage, particularly before advanced lines become automatic.
contentBlocks.caption: Better handling makes it easier to hold clean racing lines and correct imperfect drifts on technical courses.
contentBlocks.heading: Handling and Traction Decide How Easy the Build Is to Drive
contentBlocks.imageAlt: A Mario Kart 8 Deluxe racer takes a tight corner while drifting on a technical section of track.

contentBlocks.text:
Weight affects how strongly racers interact when they collide. Heavier combinations are harder for lighter racers to push around and can feel more stable in crowded sections.

The tradeoff is that heavier drivers and parts often give up some acceleration, handling, or Mini-Turbo in exchange for speed and weight. That can make a heavy build powerful on open sections but less forgiving after an item hit or on a technical track.

For most players, weight is something to consider after the core speed, acceleration, and Mini-Turbo balance feels right rather than a stat to maximize on its own.
contentBlocks.caption: Heavier combinations resist being pushed around, but their extra speed and weight often come with weaker recovery or Mini-Turbo.
